top_rules: VD-01 (SH-GATE-21): every inline check of non-shell files is `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- PATHSPEC | xargs -0 -r grep -H -n -e PAT -e PAT2 --`; never `grep -r`, `--include` or `rg` (18/18 cells red+green on GNU 3.11/3.12, busybox 1.37, uutils 26.04, Git Bash; the old form is masked in 17/18 on busybox).

VD-03: grep inside a check uses only `-E -F -e -H -n -l -L -c -o -q -s -v -w -x -i --`; `-r -R --include --exclude* -P -z -Z -U -I --null --no-messages` are banned (unrecognized or silently ignored on busybox).

VD-05: every cell block opens with a PREFLIGHT line that prints when git, xargs or grep is missing or the work tree is unusable (not a repo, dubious ownership), because the git-fed shape fails open with rc 0 and empty stdout.
VD-06: a cell passes only when stdout AND stderr are empty; never judge by exit status through xargs (grep 1 and grep 2 both become 123; `grep -L` is inverted on busybox) and never add `2>/dev/null`.

VD-04: quote every pathspec; `'*.ext'` matches at any depth, an exact basename is `':(glob)**/NAME'` (bare `'Makefile'` is root-only, `'*Makefile'` also hits `NotMakefile`), exclusions are `':(exclude)DIR'`.
VD-07: xargs-fed greps carry `-0 -r`, `-H`, `-n` and a trailing `--` (a file named `-x.sh` or a one-file batch breaks them otherwise); one `-e` per alternative, no pipe character in a pattern.

VD-09: lookaround, `-z`, multi-line or step-scoped checks go to `checks/NAME.sh` as POSIX awk (python3 is absent from every stock image; the 3 structural SH-CI cells are red/green as 9-12 line awk on all five hosts).

VD-08: no verification command in a markdown table cell (an unescaped pipe truncates the cell, `\|` is a literal in raw ERE); and VD-10: script checks list to a file, fail closed on an empty scope, and map exits 0/1/69/74/78/79 (`vd-check.sh`, 9/9 faults correct).
surprises: The git-fed shape moves the silent failure upstream: git missing (stock ubuntu:24.04, alpine:3.22, busybox:1.37 have no git), not a repo, or dubious ownership in a root container on a bind mount all give rc 0, empty stdout, error only on stderr; likewise a missing shfmt inside SH-GATE-09 files() and a missing rg.

On Git Bash 2.40 (MSYS grep 3.0, text mode) `grep -l -e $'\r'` does not see CRLF at all (`grep -U` and awk BINMODE=3 do), so the CR check in shell-gate.md:140 and SH-GATE-15 is a silent false green there; `$'\r'` also does not exist in dash (MISS on ubuntu sh). Only ShellCheck SC1017 saves the gate.

ubuntu:24.04 ships grep 3.11, not 3.12 as the brief says; 3.12 is ubuntu:26.04, whose uutils 0.10.0 covers coreutils only (tr cut head wc od sort mktemp cat ls) while grep, xargs, find, sed, diff and awk stay GNU/mawk, so uutils never touches the part of the shape that carries the verdict.

xargs flattens grep exit 1 (no match) and exit 2 (error) to 123, and `grep -L` exit status is inverted between GNU (plant 123, twin 0) and busybox (plant 0, twin 123); exit status is not usable as a verdict anywhere in the rewritten shape.

The shipped catalog is far larger than the map's '232 blocks / 497 rows': at 88d5e14, 1162 lines use --include/--exclude and 542 use rg (swift-quality 226, cmake-build 165, bazel-quality 116 for --include; rust-quality 269, typescript-quality 149 for rg), and 1532 table rows carry commands, 69 with an escaped pipe; owner must decide label-versus-rewrite for the sibling sets (M-X-05 option 2).

A checker rule requiring an explicit directory operand on every grep will reject the binding shape (xargs supplies the operands); it must exempt xargs-fed greps and allow the bracketed literal `[|]` used by the table-cell check.

top_rules: SH-ERR-07: enable check-set-e-suppressed (SC2310) in .shellcheckrc and leave check-extra-masked-returns (SC2312) out. Fleet counts: SC2310 62 sites, 3 actionable. SC2312 191 sites, 2 strict defects.

SH-ERR-10 (extended): never eval/cd/exec with a "$(cmd)" word in installer, CI or dev scripts; capture first. The G-MASK grep returns exactly the 8 fleet lines (2 real, 6 exempt eval snippets), 0 noise.

SH-ERR-29: no shopt -s nullglob or failglob at the top level, in a prologue, or in a sourced library. nullglob turns ls into a cwd listing, grep into a stdin read, and find -delete into a cwd delete. failglob exits 0 without set -e.

SH-ERR-30: contain any glob shopt in a subshell or a save/restore pair. A function leaves it on (8 of 8 bash) and local - does not restore a shopt. SH-EXP-21's 'function or subshell' wording is wrong for the function half.

SH-ERR-31 (joint with SH-EXP-21): the empty-glob contract is set -- ./*.x; [ -e "$1" ] || [ -L "$1" ] || exit 79. It gives exit 79 on 11 of 11 POSIX shells and 8 of 8 bash. [ -e ] alone hides dangling symlinks.

SH-ERR-22: the re-raise must reset the traps (trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM) before kill -s "$1" "$$". It dies of the signal on dash, both busybox ashes, bash 3.2 and 5.3. Without the reset it recurses into SIGSEGV on four of those.

SH-ERR-16/19 Windows row: Git Bash 5.2.15 gives 130/143/129 to a bash parent. A native parent sees an untrapped or re-raised signal as N<<8 (TERM 3840, INT 512), while exit 143 stays 143. Decode with kill -l, never a literal above 143.

SH-ERR-25 (X5): new gates use the SH-GATE-08 table. The 66/70 carve-out is frozen to 16 existing Swift sites in 7 scripts: 7 map mechanically, 9 need a design choice. Renumbering also touches 23 doc lines in 8 files.
surprises: SC2310 cannot be satisfied by repairing the callee. A function with || return on every step still triggers it at the call site, so all 62 fleet sites carry a directive or a restructure permanently. ShellCheck 0.11.0 has no baseline option.
A nested .shellcheckrc replaces its parent instead of merging. A directory-level SC2312 opt-in that omits enable=check-set-e-suppressed silently drops SC2310 for that directory.

The Cygwin runtime byte-swaps the exit status for a non-Cygwin parent (pinfo.cc:231-233). A native Windows parent (PowerShell 5.1, cmd, node) sees a Git Bash signal death as signal<<8, so the Linux-style [ $rc -gt 128 ] then kill -l $rc decode fails. MSYS also numbers USR1, BUS, CHLD, CONT, STOP and TSTP differently.

Omitting trap - before the re-raise makes the handler recurse into SIGSEGV on dash, both busybox ashes and bash 5.3, with 5.7k to 27.6k handler runs. The earlier TR claim that the inline re-raise exits 0 on ksh93u+m 1.0.10 is wrong: it exits 1.

failglob without set -e is not fail-closed. It skips only the failing command, or the whole if / { } group / && || list, and the script exits 0. It also kills the [ -e ] || continue guard before the guard runs. No ShellCheck 0.11.0 check (-o all included) flags a prologue shopt nullglob or an unguarded glob loop.
The SC2312 '150 vs 191' dispute is a scope difference: 150 sites sit in set -e files, 41 more sit in files with no set -e. Also 79% of SC2312 sites are under test/ or tests/ paths.

Run Test-CommandResolves only on the target host and pair it with the 5.1 parse and smoke run. It is blind to .NET members and parameter values: [IO.Path]::GetRelativePath, [Math]::Clamp and -Encoding utf8NoBOM all throw on 5.1 and exit 0.
surprises: about_Character_Encoding says the engine reads source as ANSI without a BOM. That is true of 5.1 only: 7.4.7 and 7.6.6 on a cp1252 host read BOM-less UTF-8 correctly.

-Encoding Default is accepted on 7.x although the 7.6 Out-File value list omits it, and it flips meaning: cp1252 on 5.1, UTF-8 without BOM on 7.x. New-ModuleManifest and Export-Clixml are also UTF-8 without BOM on Windows 7.x, while the docs say non-Windows only for the manifest.

X8 is a non-conflict on 5.1. Out-File -Encoding utf8 -Append writes its BOM only into an empty file, so it composes with AppendAllText in both orders. Add-Content adapts to an existing UTF-16 file; Out-File -Append never adapts.

The previously shipped PS-GATE-01 wrapper (analyzer-profile) was too strict: it exited 2 on valid IncludeRules-only settings. dotnet's real defect is 3 misspelled rule names that PSSA ignores without a message, so those rules have never run.

In the 7.x native boundary $OutputEncoding is UTF-8 but [Console]::OutputEncoding stays at the OEM code page (437 here). `child > file` preserves bytes on 7.4+, but `child | Out-File` and `| Set-Content` re-encode cp437 mojibake.

-Encoding oem follows the system OEM code page (GetOEMCP=437), not the console code page (chcp 850 left the bytes unchanged) and not the culture OEM code page (850), identically on 5.1, 7.4.7 and 7.6.6.

surprises: trap -p DEBUG returns empty inside a file loaded with '.', so a DEBUG chain that reads the old trap silently drops the user's trap unless the emitter's output is eval'd at the rc top level.
bash-preexec 0.7.0 switches to PS0 on bash 5.3, so any emitter DEBUG trap fires twice per command there (x10 against x5).

ble.sh saves and unsets PROMPT_COMMAND at attach and restores it around commands, so a PROMPT_COMMAND hook appended after ble-attach is discarded; ocx's bash prompt hook (hook.rs:204-233) uses that exact append (mechanism measured, ocx binary not run).

Percent doubling in cmd SET is correct only in a batch file; on stdin and FOR /F input the doubled form is stored literally, so a value with % has no single correct form per channel.
fish 3.6.0 and 4.0.2 load a completion only when the command resolves on PATH, while 4.7.0 and 4.9.3 load it regardless; plus zsh has no zero-rc user-scope completion location at all.

top_rules: PS-SEC-01: compare the SHA-256 (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath) to an expected digest before Expand-Archive, ExtractToDirectory or ExtractToFile, and fail closed on a mismatch or an empty digest.
PS-SEC-03: never claim verification the delivered .ps1 does not perform. The grimoire front-door SHA-256 claim is false for PowerShell and true for sh, so remove the claim or add the check.
PS-SEC-09: an iex-delivered script has no exit inside functions and no break as an exit. Functions throw or return a status, and one guarded exit sits at script top level (this amends PS-ERR-05).

PS-SEC-04: extract zips only with ZipFile.ExtractToDirectory or a per-entry loop that rejects rooted, drive-letter and .. entries. A hand-rolled Join-Path plus ExtractToFile writes outside the destination.
PS-SEC-02: take the expected digest from a source other than the archive's own release (embedded in the script, or a manifest on another origin). A same-release sidecar only catches corruption.
PS-SEC-05: pass -LiteralPath to Get-FileHash and Expand-Archive. With -Path, a file like ocx[1].zip is treated as a wildcard and returns no result and no error on all three engines.
PS-SEC-06: touch SecurityProtocol only on Desktop edition, only when the value is not SystemDefault, and assign exactly 3072 (-bor 12288 when Tls13 exists). Never assign Ssl3 or Tls.
PS-SEC-07: document the one-liner as irm <url> | iex or iwr -UseBasicParsing <url> | iex, never (iwr ...).Content | iex, which is a silent no-op on octet-stream.
surprises: PS-ERR-05's detection formula $null -eq $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path throws under Set-StrictMode -Version Latest when the script is iex-delivered. www-setup sets StrictMode Latest at install.ps1:63, so adopting the formula verbatim would break it. [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($PSCommandPath) is safe.
The scoop idiom ($Global:LASTEXITCODE = $c; break) survives an interactive prompt but swallows the failure in a non-interactive host. The step exits 0 and the wrapper trailer is never reached.

Expand-Archive wrote nothing outside the destination for ../ entries on 5.1, 7.4.7 and 7.6.6, so the zip-slip hazard is the hand-rolled loop, not the cmdlet. It errors with a misleading 'Cannot find path'.

(Invoke-WebRequest ...).Content | iex is a silent no-op on application/octet-stream, which is how GitHub release assets and setup.grimoire.rs/ps1 are served. irm | iex is truncation-safe, so it needs no main() wrapper.

On 5.1, Out-File -Encoding utf8 -Append onto the runner's empty file is green (the runner consumes the BOM), but Add-Content corrupts a non-ASCII path and any mix with >> is red. This partly contradicts the blanket PS-ENC-03 advice.
The Invoke-Expression lint is a token check. Replacing iex with & ([scriptblock]::Create(...)) passes the lint with identical power, so the security value is the hash check, not the token.

top_rules: Gate every fish file with `fish --no-config --no-execute FILE` on 3.6.0 and 4.9.3 (parse a file, never -c); it is blind to bash-isms, so add the grep set C1-C17.
fish has no errexit: check $status explicitly and use `if not`, never an or...and chain (it returns 1 when the test passes).
Call exit-ing helpers in statement position only; exit inside if/while/pipeline/function-condition stops with status 0.
Cleanup = global temp var + `--on-event fish_exit` handler + INT/TERM/HUP `--on-signal` handlers that rm, remove themselves and re-raise via `kill -s SIG $fish_pid`.
Use `command -q X; or ...`, not `||`, as a probe on fish <=4.0.2 (RHS skipped).
conf.d placement is idempotent: one rewritten file, fixed-name handlers, `fish_add_path --path`, no `set -U`, no `set -gxa PATH`, no theme or `__fish_initialized` writes.
Quote values for fish by escaping backslash first, then the single quote; never reuse the POSIX quoter (mise and starship lose data).
Supported range 3.6.0 to 4.9.3: no `{ }`, `|&`, `string pad -C`, `status language`, no master-only `$(cmd)` in command position; detect versions numerically or via `status test-feature`.
Never run shellcheck or shfmt on .fish files (SC1071); discover fish files separately.
Quote `test` operands, guard path variables before destructive globs, assert on exit status not fish error text, and test with littlecheck.
surprises: fish `exit` inside a function used as an `if not` / `while` / pipeline condition is demoted to a plain stop with status 0 on all four versions; www-setup works around it, nothing gates it.

A `--on-signal` handler that calls `exit N` never delivers N to the parent; only a handler that removes itself and re-raises with `kill -s SIG $fish_pid` does, and HUP re-raise gives 129 only from 4.7.0.
`nosuch || rhs` skipped the right-hand side on 3.6.0 and 4.0.2 (fixed 4.7.0), so `||` probes are unsafe at the Debian 12/13 floor.
mise and starship use the POSIX quoter for fish and corrupt values with backslashes (trailing backslash makes the file unparsable); direnv, oh-my-posh and ocx are correct.

Fleet defects: www-setup install.fish has three mktemp calls with no cleanup handler (lines 474, 542, 599), and the ocx fish stamp file leaks on TERM/INT/HUP (hook.rs:328-336); upstream fish master fails its own `fish -n` on 4.9.3 because of `$(...)` in command position.
A bare `fish_add_path DIR` in conf.d silently writes a universal `fish_user_paths` into fish_variables on all four versions; `--path` is the idempotent form.

top_rules: SH-NU-02: gate every nu file with nu-gate.nu --strict on the floor and ceiling nu; bare --ide-check exits 0 on a parse error and sees no deprecation, removed command or fall-through.
SH-NU-03: prefix externals with ^; a bareword that is not a builtin or custom command is a defect (removed `size` ran GNU binutils and exited 0 with a wrong answer).
SH-NU-06: pick version-specific nu files with `const f = (if (version | get minor) >= N {..}); source $f` (nu >= 0.102.0), never a runtime `if` around `source`, because the parser reads both files.
SH-NU-01: declare `# nu-range: floor..ceiling` (today 0.105.1..0.116.1) and run the gate on both ends again on every new nu minor.
SH-NU-10: nu cleanup is capture with `try {..; 0} catch {..}`, clean up, then `exit $code`; helpers raise `error make` and only the entry point exits.
SH-NU-12: never leave an external in tail position of `try`; it hangs past 65536 bytes on nu 0.112.1..0.116.1, so put `| complete` inside.
SH-ELV-02: gate elvish with -compileonly plus a stderr deprecation check plus a removed-name denylist, because removed commands compile and fail only at run time.
SH-ELV-06: elvish cleanup is `defer` inside the owning fn or `try..finally`, re-exiting with `$e[reason][exit-status]`; defer is skipped by `exit` and neither shell cleans up on SIGTERM/SIGHUP.
surprises: Raw `nu --ide-check` exits 0 on a parse error and is blind to deprecations, removed commands and fall-through; `nu-check` prints `false` with exit 0 unless given --debug.
Removed `"abc" | size` silently ran GNU binutils `size`, and with an `a.out` in the cwd it exited 0 with a wrong table on both 0.105.1 and 0.116.1.

A nu external in tail position of `try` hangs forever once it writes more than 65536 bytes (nu 0.112.1..0.116.1; fine on <=0.111.0). No upstream issue was found, and www-setup install.nu:148-151 already works around it.
nu `try..finally` exists from 0.111.0 but misbehaves until 0.116.0: finally ran twice on 0.111.0 and the script continued past a failed external on 0.114.1.

The nushell book contradicts itself on startup order (overview puts login.nu last, numbered list puts it at step 23). Measured on 0.105.1 and 0.116.1: login.nu loads before autoload, and `nu -c` / `nu script.nu` load no autoload at all.

top_rules: SEC-01: never put a secret on argv; use curl -K - / -H @file / --password-stdin, because /proc/<pid>/cmdline is 0444 and ps prints it.
SEC-04: scrub BASH_ENV/ENV at the invoker (env -u BASH_ENV -u ENV), not inside the script; bash honours BASH_ENV even under --noprofile --norc, the other 10 POSIX shells and bash-as-sh ignore it.
SEC-05: extend PATH as PATH="$d${PATH:+:$PATH}" and never leave an empty, '.' or relative entry; a NULL PATH is cwd on bash 3.2-5.3 alike (5.3 NEWS item p only codifies it).
SEC-06: write '. ./lib.sh' or '. "$dir/lib.sh"', never a bare name; bash 3.2-5.3, busybox ash 1.37 and yash fall back to the cwd, dash does not, so the bug hides on Debian CI.
SEC-07: never source or eval a config another principal can write; parse KEY=VALUE with read plus a case allow-list.
SEC-08: put -- before every data operand and ./ before every glob (rm, tar, ssh, git, cp, mv); ssh -oProxyCommand, git --upload-pack and tar --checkpoint-action still execute code on current tools.
SEC-10: validate any identifier from data before declare/printf -v/read/[[ -v ]]/${!k} as well as arithmetic; all execute a[$(cmd)] on bash 3.2-5.3 and array_expand_once only narrows it.
SEC-11: lock with mkdir/set -C/ln, probe flock, and never auto-break a stale mkdir lock (rmdir+mkdir and mv-aside both elect 1-7 owners).
surprises: No safe shell-only stale-lock takeover exists: both rmdir+mkdir and mv-aside produced 1-7 winners per round with 20 contenders on dash, busybox ash 1.37 and bash 5.3, so the rule becomes report-the-holder-and-exit.

bash 5.3's NULL PATH NEWS item is not new behaviour: execution is identical on 3.2-5.3; only command -v/type output (./planted vs absolute) and the not-found text differ. unset PATH still searches cwd on bash and busybox ash but not dash/mksh/ksh93/yash/posh/zsh.

The dynamic-name reach is wider than SH-EXP-19 lists: read -r "$k", declare "$k=v", ${!k}, printf -v (4.2+) and [[ -v $k ]] (4.4+) execute a[$(cmd)]; bash 5.3 array_expand_once stops only let, printf -v and read.

sudo-rs 0.2.8/0.2.13 silently ignore bare sudo -E and --preserve-env (warning, exit unchanged); the oils corpus uses sudo -E, while k3s install.sh:805 already uses the portable --preserve-env=VAR. Denial messages differ between implementations, so scripts must key off exit codes.

posh 0.14.1 corrupts builtin arguments under 30 concurrent busy-wait subshells (wait: invalid option, 4/4 runs), so the SH-USER-06 lock matrix must cap posh at N<=6; also cross-filesystem mv is measurably non-atomic (4-7 torn reads of ~185) and GLOBIGNORE imported from the environment is never honoured on bash 3.2-5.3 despite the manual's privileged-mode text.

An unset BASH_ENV inside a script (as in my own first twin) is a no-op for that run, and PS4 import runs code for non-root on every bash 3.2-5.3; only root gains protection from 4.4. GitHub Actions' default bash --noprofile --norc invocation still sources BASH_ENV.

top_rules: Route a failure on exit code, first stderr line and interpreter identity together; the same CR shebang gives rc 126 or 127 and four different texts by launcher.
Rule out a CR byte first on any 126/127 for a file that exists: `git ls-files --eol -- . | awk` is red on the plant and empty on the twin.
Never answer `set: Illegal option -o pipefail` with `|| true` or a bash shebang flip; dash 0.5.12-2/-6ubuntu5 and posh abort regardless, only the SH-DIAL-07 subshell probe is safe.
Decode signal deaths with `[ "$rc" -gt 128 ]` and `kill -l`, never a literal 141/143; ksh93u+m gives 269/271 and yash 397/399.
Guard empty arrays under `set -u` as `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}`; the unbound error hits bash 3.2, 4.0 and 4.2, not only 3.2.

A port starts with a baseline matrix run and ends with byte-identical output on every bash 3.2-5.3 equal to the pre-port newest-bash output; ShellCheck is green throughout and proves nothing about 3.2.
Judge the git-fed denylist by its output, not its status: the final `xargs` returns 123 on a clean tree.
Every emitter needs a named quoter per (target, context) and a corpus round trip that goes red on a shared quoter; yash needs LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 at process start or the test is a false red.
surprises: The wave-2 PS-ERR-05 iex-detection formula `$null -eq $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path` throws under `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` on 5.1, 7.4 and 7.6.6, and www-setup sets StrictMode Latest at install.ps1:63; `[string]::IsNullOrEmpty($PSCommandPath)` is the working form (rule text needs an amendment).
Three house SKILL.md files already exceed the 500-line ceiling (nix-flake-release 507, swift-upgrade 506, swift-release 505), so the 'under 500' rule is unenforced in the catalog today.

On bash 3.2 `declare -A` prints 'invalid option' but returns rc 0 and leaves an indexed array, `mapfile` is command-not-found yet the script continues, and bash 4.4 exits 0 with a silently wrong `EPOCHREALTIME` (timer=0); ShellCheck 0.11.0 is green on all of it, so only the denylist plus a bash:3.2 run can gate a port.
The Git Bash `cmd /c` hang has silent siblings: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 cmd //c` still hangs, and with stdin closed `cmd /c` prints only the banner and exits 0 with no output.

The CR-in-shebang text depends on the launching shell and bash version (bash 5.2 says 'cannot execute: required file not found' rc 127, 5.3 reverted to 'bad interpreter' rc 126), so ubuntu-latest moving to bash 5.3 changes what CI logs show.
